subject: Clarification: data custody routing and transient cross-region processing for HelixCare
messages:
From: Dana Park <dana.park@helixcare.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixCare Legal <legal@helixcare.com>, Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@cloudops.io>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on custody routing + transient cross-region processing

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the call earlier this week. Before we proceed with the DPA addendum, a couple of clarification points from our security team that we need captured in writing:

1) Custody path: you mentioned "regional custody" for stored artifacts, but we need specifics about which components may briefly leave our selected region (US/EU/APAC) during operational flows (e.g., cache warmups, model failovers, cold starts). Please list exact data paths and the maximum dwell time outside region.

2) Transient processing window: our requirement is strict — any transient cross-border processing for PHI must be time-bounded. Can you confirm Redwood's maximum allowed window (we asked for 24-72h previously) and whether that is configurable per-account?

3) Subprocessors: we need an up-to-date roster that clearly marks which subprocessors may touch ephemeral copies, and which are strictly control-plane only. A one‑page mapping (role -> company -> region) would help.

4) Evidence: what artifacts can you produce during onboarding to prove those constraints (audit logs, KMS key IDs, routing traces)?

We'd like to resolve these items this week so legal can finish the DPA review. Attaching a short checklist from our side (see referenced doc in body).

Appreciate the help — let me know if a quick sync with engineering is easier.

Thanks,
Dana Park
Head of Security Programs
HelixCare

Attachments: helixcare_onboarding_questions.docx (referenced)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on custody routing + transient cross-region processing

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Below is our consolidated position at a high level; I can follow up with the technical runbook and the subprocessor roster (attached) by EOD. If helpful, we can also do a 30‑minute technical call with Karthik and Oliver.

High-level answers:
- Custody path: persistent customer data (objects, embeddings, model checkpoints) is pinned to the customer-selected region for storage. Short-lived artifacts used for inference (KV caches, prefix caches, temp tensors) may be routed to a neighbouring region only in two narrow cases: (a) cache warmup for a new edge instance; (b) automated failover where capacity in-region is exhausted.
- Max dwell time: our operational SLO for any transient cross-region processing is 72 hours by default; most incidents complete <24 hours. We support per-customer stricter limits ( configurable to 24h ) under Dedicated or Private plans via a routing policy.
- Subprocessors: attached is the current roster (helixcare_subprocessors_202704.pdf). We mark "ephemeral-access" subprocessors (edge CDN, caching infra) vs "control-plane-only" (billing, analytics).
- Evidence: we can provide per-request routing traces, KMS key IDs for region‑scoped keys, and audit logs showing egress events. For PHI workloads we recommend enabling detailed token-level telemetry so you get a traceable trail.

Next steps: I'll get the technical runbook (transient-egress-runbook_v2.docx) and a shorter one‑page mapping across roles/regions. Would you prefer those delivered to legal, or a shared Drive link?

Best,

Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helixcare_subprocessors_202704.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: data custody routing and transient cross-region processing for HelixCare

Mina / Marissa — quick technical notes to drop into the runbook before we send to HelixCare: (copying here so Mina can quote into the customer reply)

- Mechanisms that can cause transient cross-region copies:
  * KV/prefix cache replication (warm starts across edge nodes) — these caches contain inference context only and are zeroed after TTL expiry or when eviction occurs.
  * Short-lived prefetch for burst autoscaling — when traffic spikes we may pre-warm instances in a neighboring region; pre-warmed caches are populated with data only necessary for immediate inference and automatically scrubbed.
  * Emergency failover: if an entire region is degraded we spin up capacity elsewhere and stream minimal state for continuity.

- Dwell-time enforcement: we implement a topology watcher that enforces the configured per-account dwell-time ceiling; it emits an alert at T+48h and auto-scrubs at T+72h if the artifact is still present. For Dedicated customers we can set hard tenancy — artifacts will be prevented from leaving region except via manual-approved breakglass.

- Subprocessor roles: separate list we will include in the PDF, but call out: edge caching provider (ephemeral), object storage provider (persistent), monitoring vendor (control-plane metrics only), KMS/HSM provider (key management, region-scoped).

- Audit evidence: we can export (a) routing traces correlated to request IDs, (b) audit-log slices (UTC) for any specified time window, (c) signed KMS key IDs and Cloud provider region tags.

If HelixCare wants a 24h max instead of 72h, we should confirm pricing/operational impact — smaller failover windows increase cache-miss rates and potentially latency/cost. Suggest we offer both a standard (72h) and an SLA-graded 24h option for their review.

-Karthik
Principal, Inference Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification: data custody routing and transient cross-region processing for HelixCare

Dana —

Following internal technical input, attached are the two artifacts you requested: the subprocessor roster (PDF) and the transient egress runbook (DOCX). Key points summarized for legal review below — please let me know which items you want us to put directly in the DPA addendum language.

Summary (customer-facing):
- Persistent custody: all customer persistent objects and model artifacts are stored in the customer-selected region. Persistent storage egress is blocked by policy unless explicit export is requested via onboarding flow.
- Transient processing: KV/prefix caches and pre-warm artifacts may be placed in neighbouring regions only for warmup or failover; default configured ceiling is 72 hours, with automatic alerts at 48h and forced scrubbing at 72h.
- Configurability: For Dedicated/Private customers we can enforce a 24h ceiling or fully restrict cross-region placement. This is enforced via routing policies and our topology watcher.
- Subprocessors: the attached roster marks roles (ephemeral vs control-plane) and regions. The list is current as of 2027-04-15; we commit to 30-day notice for roster changes.
- Evidence types: routing traces (per request ID), audit-log slices (time-bounded), and KMS key metadata are available for onboarding and periodic review.

Requested next steps from HelixCare: please confirm whether you need the 24h hard ceiling option for PHI in the DPA addendum or whether the 72h default with monitoring + 30-day subprocessor notice is acceptable. If you want the 24h ceiling, we will prepare pricing/ops impact in a short appendix.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute technical Q&A with Karthik and Oliver next week.

Thanks again —

Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
